source.title: More Thinking, Less Talking: Internalizing Deliberative Safety into LLM Parameters
source.authors: Guan Wang; Xuehai Tang; Biyu Zhou; Ji-Zhong Han; Songlin Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates whether low-rank parameter updates can reproduce SCoT-related safety effects, using a different method from the cited fine-tuning and few-token studies.
record.gate_note: The paper tests low-rank internalization and causal components involved in SCoT safety correction. It does not test harmful or benign fine-tuning erosion, per-token KL concentration, compliant prefilling, or decoding changes. The GCG attack results do not establish that GCG is a suffix attack in this text.
record.test_reason: The paper is a defense paper: HIAR internalizes SCoT safety reasoning into low-rank FFN LoRA adapters. It cites shallow alignment (Qi et al., 2024) only as motivation. Its low-rank results show that a low-rank update can add SCoT-like safety to a model. That measures the authors' own method against rank. It does not show that an aligned model's existing safety lives in a small set of weights or ranks (V5). It runs no harmful or benign fine-tuning erosion, no per-token KL, no prefilling and no deepening test. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SCoT's corrective effect is localized in FFN layers and is low-rank, so it can be internalized with layer-wise LoRA (HIAR). They report about 43% lower ASR than strong baselines, with negligible capability loss and no exposed reasoning trace.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs SCoT supervision and trains or analytically computes FFN LoRA updates to internalize it. It does not reproduce harmful or benign fine-tuning erosion, aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement, or compliant-prefill experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported rank-4 internalization result is described as nearly matching contextual SCoT; the paper also reports a rank sweep, but its model-specific values are only in figures. It states that rank 10 achieves most defensive gain overall.

fits_no_version.finding: A rank-constrained (as low as r=4) analytic FFN update reproduces the ASR of explicit SCoT conditioning. HIAR's defensive gain saturates by about rank 10 across four small models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety corrections induced by a safety chain-of-thought context can be added to a model through a low-rank FFN update.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-10 singular vectors explain over 96% of SCoT-induced hidden-state deviations, while a random-context control has a flatter spectrum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SCoT-induced hidden-state corrections lie in a low-dimensional subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching post-FFN states from the SCoT run into middle-to-late layers cuts ASR to near the reference level. Post-attention patching has a much smaller effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The FFN is the main causal locus of SCoT safety correction.

record.code_released: The paper says code and data will be released upon acceptance; URL not stated.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2026
record.problems: The rank-1-to-10 validation and smaller-model rank sweep are presented in figures without numeric values in the text; most model-specific rank-sweep results therefore cannot be determined from the supplied text. The preliminary low-rank validation does not identify its BaseModel. The paper itself notes limited model scale and architectural diversity for some experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also states that protection levels gradually level off when comparing ranks 50 and 100, but the text does not identify the subject or give a separately assignable condition/value for that statement. Main jailbreak-defense tables are not recorded as V5 rows because they report HIAR defense performance rather than isolate the effect of parameter rank.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling or decoding attack. GCG/AutoDAN/PAIR/PAP ASRs are reported only as baselines for the defense comparison.
Does not test whether an aligned model's existing safety is carried by a few weights or ranks. It only shows that a low-rank update can add SCoT-like safety.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No test of whether safety extends beyond the first tokens. HIAR is not framed or measured as deepening across positions.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's 'No Defense' baselines report high jailbreak ASR. Examples: Llama-3-8B-Instruct GCG 30.2% and PAP 92.4% (Table 1); DeepSeek-R1 GCG 86.32% (Table 7). These are baseline comparators for the defense, and the text does not describe GCG as a suffix attack. If the claim owners want baseline attack ASRs on aligned models as V4 evidence, they could be added as rows, but the study does not frame them as a test. The model in the Section 3 analyses is unidentified ('BaseModel'). Code is not released.

versions.untested_parts: Whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples removes refusals.
Whether ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Whether compliant prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes bypass safety; the text does not identify its GCG results as suffix attacks.
The study tests low-rank updates that internalize SCoT safety effects, not whether a small set of parameters in an already aligned model originally carries its safety behavior.
Whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
Whether safety training spreads safety beyond the first response tokens and whether that depth withstands bypass attempts.
